nsduh-2024.name: SAMHSA: 2024 National Survey on Drug Use and Health, annual national report (U.S.)

any-mental-illness.name: Any mental illness (AMI) in the past year, adults
any-mental-illness.passage: In 2024, 23.4 percent of adults aged 18 or older (or 61.5 million people) had AMI in the past year.

serious-mental-illness.name: Serious mental illness (SMI) in the past year, adults
serious-mental-illness.passage: In 2024, 5.6 percent of adults aged 18 or older (or 14.6 million people) had SMI in the past year.

major-depressive-episode.name: Major depressive episode (MDE) in the past year, adults
major-depressive-episode.passage: In 2024, 8.2 percent of adults aged 18 or older (or 21.4 million people) had a past year MDE.

anxiety-symptoms.name: Moderate or severe symptoms of generalized anxiety disorder, adults
anxiety-symptoms.passage: Among adults aged 18 or older in 2024, 7.4 percent (or 19.4 million people) had moderate or severe symptoms of GAD

substance-use-disorder.name: Substance use disorder (SUD) in the past year
substance-use-disorder.passage: In 2024, 48.4 million people aged 12 or older (or 16.8 percent of the population) had an SUD in the past year

serious-thoughts-of-suicide.name: Serious thoughts of suicide in the past year, adults
serious-thoughts-of-suicide.passage: In 2024, 5.5 percent of adults aged 18 or older (or 14.3 million people) had serious thoughts of suicide in the past year.

suicide-attempt.name: Attempted suicide in the past year, adults
suicide-attempt.passage: In 2024, 0.8 percent of adults aged 18 or older (or 2.2 million people) attempted suicide in the past year.

unmet-need-mental-health.name: Perceived unmet need for mental health treatment, adults with AMI not treated
unmet-need-mental-health.passage: Of the 61.5 million adults aged 18 or older in 2024 who had AMI in the past year ( Figure 57 ), slightly less than half (29.5 million people) did not receive mental health treatment in the past year ( Table A.66A ). Among these 29.5 million adults with AMI in the past year who did not receive mental health treatment, 21.0 percent (or 6.1 million people) perceived an unmet need for mental health treatment in the past year

treatment-cost.name: Reason for not getting mental health treatment: would cost too much
treatment-cost.passage: The second most common reason for not receiving treatment was thinking treatment would cost too much (65.2 percent).
